name: Structures and building safety
description: Site inspection records, incident and stop-work orders, OSHA report records, structural monitoring and post-disaster building evaluation: rapid and detailed evaluation forms, assignment logs and the INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE and UNSAFE placards. For contractors, engineers, building departments and every organization that has a building, a trench or a crane in a hazard.
outsideParties: the OSHA area office or the state occupational safety plan
the fire department's technical rescue team or the state urban search and rescue task force
the city or county building department
the utility and the one-call center

advisorRoles.name: Structural engineer (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains what a monitoring series, a crack or a lean means, and what an evaluation can and cannot say about a structure.

advisorRoles.name: Construction safety director (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains stop-work authority, the competent person's duties and the OSHA reporting clocks.

advisorRoles.name: Building safety evaluator (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains how a rapid evaluation is done, how a placard is chosen and what makes two teams disagree.

glossary.definition: Identifies hazards at the work area and is authorized to take prompt corrective action; inspects excavations daily.
The design engineer who decides structural adequacy, repair and shoring.
Declares a building unsafe, authorizes placards and decides re-entry.
INSPECTED (green), RESTRICTED USE (yellow) or UNSAFE (red); the building at the time it was evaluated.
A short look at one building to recommend a placard; not a structural analysis.
Runs a critical crane pick against the lift plan and the load chart.

productConventions: Placards and categories are written as words (INSPECTED, RESTRICTED USE, UNSAFE), never as a color alone.
Monitoring thresholds have an alarm and an action level; state the unit, the sensor and the time.
Every product is marked as an exercise and is not a safety evaluation of any real structure.
realismRules: The competent person, superintendent or safety director stops work; the engineer of record decides structural adequacy; only the building official declares a building unsafe.
A work-related fatality is reported to OSHA within 8 hours; an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours.

Excavations need a protective system unless in stable rock or under 5 feet with no sign of a cave-in; inspect daily and after rain; a trench 4 feet or deeper needs an exit within 25 feet; workers leave the hazard until precautions are taken.
Do not state a depth rule for engineered trench systems.
Rescue is run by the fire department; the contractor supplies drawings, equipment and a structural opinion.

decisionForms.label: Stop work
decisionForms.description: Stop all or part of the work on the site. The competent person, superintendent and safety director may stop work.

decisionForms.label: Evacuate the site or an adjacent building
decisionForms.description: Order people out of the site, a neighboring building or the street.

decisionForms.label: Call 911 and request rescue
decisionForms.description: Call 911 and ask for the help the situation needs. Rescue tactics belong to the fire department.

decisionForms.label: Set the exclusion zone
decisionForms.description: Keep people out of the area that could be hit by a further collapse or a falling load.

decisionForms.label: Shore or stabilize
decisionForms.description: Ask for shoring or stabilize a load or structure. The engineer of record decides adequacy.

fields.label: Action
choices: Hold in place and wait for the engineer

decisionForms.label: Shut off or isolate a utility
decisionForms.description: Close a valve, open a breaker or ask the utility to isolate a line.

decisionForms.label: Notify OSHA, the owner, the insurer or the building official
decisionForms.description: Report or notify. A work-related fatality is reported to OSHA within 8 hours; an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours.

decisionForms.label: Post a placard
decisionForms.description: Post a placard from the information in the building record. The placard describes the building at the time it was evaluated.

decisionForms.label: Issue an unsafe building order
decisionForms.description: Only the building official declares a building unsafe.

decisionForms.label: Assign an evaluation team
decisionForms.description: Send a team to an area or a class of buildings.

decisionForms.label: Release a public statement
decisionForms.description: Say what is known, what is not, and what people should do.

metrics.label: Stop work before the monitoring reading passes the action level (reading in the unit above the action level)
Time from the first sign to stop work and evacuation
OSHA, owner and insurer notices against their clocks
Collapse to 911, exclusion zone and shoring, and secondary hazards controlled
Placards against the ground truth, priority order and throughput
Agreement on the structure status and the exclusion zone

criticalTasks: Stop work and clear the site before anyone has proof of failure when a threshold is crossed.
Coordinate the contractor, owner, engineer, building department and fire department on one status of the structure.
Call 911 and request rescue at once, and support rescue with drawings, equipment and a structural opinion.
Control secondary hazards that endanger rescuers (gas, fire, a falling element).
Keep streets and access routes clear of the exclusion zone and open for responders.
Isolate or shut off a struck utility and name who confirms it is safe.
Evaluate buildings in priority order: hospitals, shelters and schools first.
Read monitoring data and decide whether a silent sensor is failed or warning.
Count buildings by placard and report the counts to the emergency operations center.
Give neighbors and the public one consistent statement about the structure and the exclusion zone.
Secure the scene, control access with a sign-in log and preserve it for investigators.
Account for every worker against the sign-in log and report a fatality to OSHA within 8 hours.
Assign evaluation teams by area and priority and keep the program record.
